newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Assembly approves birth control coverage bill.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Assembly approves birth control coverage bill.

text.p: California's state Assembly on Monday approved legislation requiring health insurers and health maintenance organizations to help cover the cost of birth control.
"This is a common sense solution to a very important problem," said the bill's author, Assemblyman Robert Hertzberg, a Democrat.

The bill, sponsored by the Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California, would require all health insurers and health plans to include coverage for a variety of birth control methods within their prescription drug benefits.

"Currently, half of all insurance and benefit plans provide no contraceptive coverage, but routinely cover abortions, sterilizations and tubal ligations -- all more dangerous and more expensive procedures," Hertzberg said.
Providing prescription contraception would cost health plans an estimated $16 a year per person, he said.
The Assembly approved the measure by 43-to-25, sending the bill to the Senate for review.
Opponents of the bill argued that the proposal was costly and inappropriate.
"This is a bad bill," said Assemblyman Bernie Richter, a Republican. "Consumers would pay at least twice as much for contraceptives because health plans would become more costly."
California Gov. Pete Wilson, a Republican, vetoed a similar bill in 1995.
